function: p. 9: TD3 learns IRS phase shifts, HAP energy beamforming and sensors' uplink power to maximize the long-term sum-rate; alignment and ZF vectors follow [6].
system: p. 4, 12: HAP with 3 energy-beamforming and 4 receive antennas; 12 sensors with 2x4 antennas; passive reflecting IRS with 20-60 elements; narrow-band, wavelength 0.4 m; full duplex.
method: p. 8-11: TD3 actor-critic deep reinforcement learning with twin critics, delayed updates and replay buffer; actor with hidden layers of 128 and 256 neurons.
data_channel: p. 4-5: custom simulator, Rician fading on all links with path loss and IRS spatial correlation, bounded CSI error model; no 3GPP model, public dataset or measurements.
test_conditions: p. 11, 13: sum-rate averaged over all episodes and time steps; separate runs for 20, 40 and 60 IRS elements; no held-out scenario or test set.
baselines: p. 11: DDPG and SAC (learned); PSO and random allocation (non-learned); compared on average sum-rate in Figs. 3-5, DRL methods only in Figs. 6-8.
metrics: p. 13-15: average sum-rate (bps/Hz) under perfect and imperfect CSI, average normalized reward, convergence over episodes, approximate complexity (Table VI).
complexity: p. 12-13: big-O per-iteration cost of actor, critic and full algorithm; Table VI lists approximate complexity, TD3 5.78e10, SAC 5.96e10, PSO 5.8e13, random 4.4e6.
q1_support: p. 4: "The Rician fading model is applied to all channel links." The links are a custom Rician simulator with path loss and a bounded CSI error model (p. 4-5); no 3GPP TR 38.901, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "the average of the sum-rate over all episodes and time steps"; no held-out scenario. M = 20, 40 and 60 are separate runs with their own batch sizes and convergence plots (p. 13), and Figs. 6-8 sweep Rmin, Pmax and cluster sizes with no stated test on unseen settings.
q3_support: p. 11: "we consider two DRL algorithms: DDPG" and "we use two non-DRL methods: random allocation and PSO"; all are compared on average sum-rate in Figs. 3(b)-5(b) (p. 13).
q4_support: p. 12: "the computational complexity of each algorithm is summarized in Table VI"; big-O expressions are on p. 12 and Table VI (p. 13) gives approximate values for TD3, DDPG, SAC, PSO and random assignment.
q5_support: p. 13: "Detailed system parameters for this deployment are provided in Tables IV and V"; the data come from the paper's own simulator and no code or data link is given (the only URLs, on p. 16, are third-party references).
notes: Included, area 3: the TD3 agent sets the HAP energy-beamforming matrix, the IRS phase shifts and the sensors' uplink power (Eq. 13, p. 9); signal-alignment and ZF vectors are computed as in [6], not learned (p. 11). DDPG and SAC are standard DRL algorithms applied to the same problem, hence q3=1. Wavelength 0.4 m (Table IV, p. 12) is the only carrier information given.
